text.p: Year-end results for Mexican builder Grupo Tribasa are expected to be weak, with net profits crippled by the company's poor operating performance, analysts said.
The company is forecast to report earnings of 0.95 pesos a share in 1996, according to a Reuters survey of five analysts, reversing a 1995 loss per share of 3.16 pesos per share.
But analysts agreed earnings per share were distorted by accounting effects such as the integrated cost of financing and earnings from of concessioned highways.

"(Results) should come in low. Already in the third quarter activity level was low and they were clear in saying they expected it to continue through the fourth quarter," UBS Securities analyst Alvaro Shiraishi said.

Although unlikely, Tribasa could have suffered a loss in operating costs, he said. In the third quarter of 1996 Tribasa's operating margins fell to 4.15 percent, compared with 14.6 percent the year before. In the second quarter operating margins were 19.1 percent.
Rafael Elias Linero, CS First Boston analyst, expects an operating loss in the fourth quarter of 181 million pesos, leaving a lean 3.3 percent operating margin for the year.

"I see operating losses because of the scarce level of work in Mexico and Chile and also because of an increase in general administration and sales expenses, because Tribasa is bidding for all types of projects in Mexico," he said.
Some analysts said Mexico's transportation sector could have registered improved growth in the final quarter of 1996, a boon for Tribasa's income from highway tolls.
Goldman Sachs analyst Christopher Hussey said the company needs financial restructuring of its toll road concessions to reduce debt and begin new projects. The restructuring is expected shortly.
